close_reason: Decision recorded: extend mime-tree to expose typed header values (MIME-vy5), then consume from jmap-mail-server. JMAP-g7wu.5 now waits on MIME-vy5 instead of on this bead.
description:
JMAP-g7wu.5 needs to implement five RFC 8621 header-form parsers (AsAddresses, AsGroupedAddresses, AsDate, AsMessageIds, AsURLs) in jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs. The mime-tree crate at ~/PROJECT/MIME/mime-tree contains internal parsers that match the required RFC 5322 ABNF, but does NOT expose them as public functions. Three non-equivalent strategies:

## (a) Add a new parser dep to jmap-mail-server Cargo.toml

Candidate crates:
- `mailparse` — popular, MIT, parses RFC 5322 headers; has been around since 2015; ~1.6k stars; covers address/group/date/message-id; URL forms need separate handling
- `email-encoding` — RustCrypto-adjacent; smaller; less complete for the 5 As* forms
- `email-address-parser` or similar focused crates — only cover one or two of the 5 forms

**Pros:** Smallest code change in jmap-mail-server. Existing well-tested implementation. No cross-repo work.
**Cons:** Adds an external dep to a workspace that has been deliberately minimal on parser deps (currently relies on mime-tree as the single MIME/header parser). Increases supply-chain attack surface. Doubles parser-implementation surface (two implementations of RFC 5322 in the same dep tree).

## (b) Extend mime-tree to make its internal parsers public

Cross-repo change at ~/PROJECT/MIME/mime-tree — promote the existing internal parser functions to `pub` (or expose via a new sub-module `mime_tree::headers::parse`). Then consume them from jmap-mail-server.

**Pros:** Single source of truth for RFC 5322 parsing in the workspace family. No new external dep. mime-tree already has these parsers — just an API-visibility change.
**Cons:** Requires a coordinated change to a sister repo (mime-tree is not in this workspace). Mark owns mime-tree but it has its own release cadence. May want a mime-tree minor-version bump.

## (c) Implement the 5 parsers from scratch in jmap-mail-server

Write RFC 5322 ABNF-compliant parsers directly in jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs (or a sibling module).

**Pros:** Zero new external deps. No cross-repo coordination. Tight control over error reporting and corner cases.
**Cons:** Hundreds of LoC. Real correctness risk on RFC 5322 ABNF edge cases (comments in addresses, obs-* productions, RFC 6532 internationalisation). Reinvents what (a) or (b) already provide. Needs an independent oracle for tests (probably OpenSSL or pyca/cryptography output, but those do not directly cover all 5 header forms).

## Recommendation

**(b)** if mime-tree changes are cheap to ship in the next month — this is the architecturally clean answer.
**(a) with `mailparse`** if mime-tree changes are not on the near-term roadmap — `mailparse` is the most mature option and the dep cost is acceptable for this scope.
**(c)** is the worst option — accept it only if (a) and (b) are both unavailable.

## What to do to resolve

1. Comment on this bead with the chosen strategy and rationale.
2. Close this bead — that unblocks JMAP-g7wu.5.
3. The autonomous loop will then pick up JMAP-g7wu.5 and execute the chosen strategy.

Note: the `human` label here is informational — bd-spin will not stop on it until the autonomous frontier is exhausted (see JMAP-j6td). It surfaces in `bd list --label human --status open` so the human can find it.
title: Decide parser strategy for the 5 RFC 5322 As* header forms (blocks JMAP-g7wu.5)
